title: Statics & Mechanics of Materials
description: Equilibrium, internal loads, stress, strain, and failure criteria as tools for safe devices, fixtures, implants, and bioreactor hardware.

outcomes.description: Compute axial, torsional, and bending stress.
Relate material response to boundary conditions.
Use safety factors with an explicit failure criterion.

lesson_objectives.description: Isolate a body and include all external reactions.
Solve force and moment balance in 2D.
Compute normal stress and elastic extension.
Check units and identify when a linear model applies.
Relate torque to shear stress in a circular shaft.
Use bending moment to predict normal stress in a beam.
Distinguish yield, ultimate, fatigue, and functional failure.
Calculate and interpret a factor of safety.
Compute the second moment of area of a hollow circular section and the maximum bending stress from a moment.
Combine axial and bending stresses at a point and calculate a safety factor against a stated failure criterion.
Explain why a hollow section is more efficient in bending than a solid one of equal area, and evaluate the limits of applying beam theory to bone and implants.
Draw a free-body diagram for a body segment and apply force and moment equilibrium to find unknown muscle and joint forces.
Resolve an angled muscle force into components and compute the resulting joint compression.
Interpret mechanical advantage and evaluate how changes in geometry and load affect muscle and joint forces.

lessons.title: Free-body diagrams and equilibrium
lessons.worked_example: A simply supported beam with a centered point load P has reactions P/2 at each support by symmetry and moment equilibrium.

lessons.title: Axial load, stress, and strain
lessons.worked_example: A 100 mm-long bar with A=10 mm², E=2 GPa, and F=20 N extends ΔL=0.1 mm under the simple axial model.

lessons.title: Torsion and bending
lessons.worked_example: A circular shaft's maximum torsional shear occurs at its outer radius; doubling radius also changes J strongly, so geometry cannot be ignored.

modules.title: Failure criteria, fatigue, and design margins

lessons.title: Failure criteria, fatigue, and design margins
lessons.worked_example: If a component's allowable load is 900 N and design load is 300 N under the stated model, the load factor is 3; the reliability meaning still depends on uncertainty and failure mode.

lessons.title: Bending of a long bone: second moment of area, combined stresses and why bones are hollow
lessons.worked_example: For r_o = 13 mm and r_i = 7 mm, I = 20546 mm⁴; 100 N·m gives 63.3 MPa bending stress, plus 5.31 MPa from a 2000 N axial load, so 68.6 MPa and a safety factor of 2.19 against 150 MPa; a solid rod of equal area would reach 96.9 MPa.

lessons.title: Force and moment equilibrium in the body: free-body diagrams of a forearm holding a load
lessons.worked_example: Moments about the elbow give a muscle force of 493.8 N for a 50 N load at 35 cm, and the joint pushes down with 428.8 N; at 80° the muscle needs 501.4 N and adds 87.1 N of compression; mechanical advantage 0.114.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added an original lesson on bending of a long bone (second moment of area, combined stresses, safety factor, hollow sections and stress shielding) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added an original lesson on force and moment equilibrium of a forearm holding a load with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Fixed number formatting that an earlier authoring step left in learner-visible text: raw exponent notation (a number written with the letter e and a power of ten) and floating-point artifacts (a decimal with a long run of trailing digits) in item statics-materials-3:bending-stress. No answer key, tolerance or objective changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: Four compact legacy units are preserved; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.
There is no authored 12–15 week schedule, substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm, cumulative final, or graded integrative project.

Practice items are short formative checks (two per prototype unit and six per original lesson); they do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery, and objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.

Of the 17 numerical answers in this package, ten require a unit, none checks significant figures and none checks dimensions; the others accept a number within a stated tolerance, with the unit optional.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.
intentionally_omitted: Full instructional sequence and summative assessments are not authored yet; the original lessons extend a partial package.
